summary: Completed backend + frontend validation for requested auth/admin/account/auctions/product-detail flows against public preview URL. All requested user-facing flows pass except one backend integration defect: CORS preflight currently rejects the app origin with 400 'Disallowed CORS origin'.

critical.issue: Preflight from https://dashboard-design-20.preview.emergentagent.com returns 400 with body 'Disallowed CORS origin' while allow_credentials headers are present.

action_items: Fix backend CORS origin matching so OPTIONS preflight for preview origin returns 200/204 (not 400).
Re-run auth/browser regression after CORS fix, especially login/forgot/reset from browser context.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py config sets CORS allow_origins=[FRONTEND_URL], but observed runtime behavior rejects the configured preview origin during preflight; verify deployed FRONTEND_URL value normalization and exact-match handling.
Auth implementation now correctly supports identifier login (email/username), one-time reset token invalidation, 5-failure lockout, and secure HttpOnly cookies.
seed_data() includes 'deepak143' admin upsert with password refresh logic; this path exists in code but password-change behavior was not force-mutated in this run.
seed_data_creation: Created temporary TEST_ users via register endpoint and generated password reset tokens during auth tests.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Validated: /admin login with deepak143, admin register hidden, forgot-password visible on both admin/customer login, customer register mismatch blocked, customer login works with provided credential, profile click routes to /account, signout works only from account page, /auctions renders place-bid-button without runtime crash, /product/iphone shows Similar Products and image zoom modal open/close. Backend pytest file for this iteration is ready for reuse.
rca of the issue: CORS preflight reproduction: OPTIONS /api/auth/login with Origin=https://dashboard-design-20.preview.emergentagent.com and Access-Control-Request-Method=POST returns 400 + 'Disallowed CORS origin'. Likely root cause is runtime allow_origins mismatch (env value mismatch, normalization, or deployment config divergence) even though application code intends explicit origin + credentials.
